matching_criterion: Acute otitis media of the right ear in a child. Any wording that names acute otitis media / middle-ear infection counts as correct; otitis externa, viral upper respiratory infection alone or mastoiditis as the final diagnosis does not.

management_reference.management: In a child without perforation or severe symptoms, watchful waiting is the usual approach, with antibiotics prescribed if symptoms persist for 1 to 3 days or the child deteriorates.
management_reference.source_quote: recommended a watchful waiting approach where clinicians were encouraged to prescribe antibiotics if symptoms persisted for 1–3 days or in case of any clinical deterioration

management_reference.management: If an antibiotic is used, oral amoxicillin is the usual first-line choice.
management_reference.source_quote: recommended oral amoxicillin as an option for first-line treatment

management_reference.management: No routine laboratory or radiographic investigations.
management_reference.source_quote: No guidelines advised routine laboratory or radiographic investigations

management_reference.management: The diagnosis rests on acute onset of symptoms, middle-ear effusion (bulging tympanic membrane or otorrhoea) and tympanic membrane inflammation on examination.
management_reference.source_quote: acute onset of symptoms (ie, otalgia, fever), (2) evidence of middle ear (ME) effusion

management_scoring_note: Only items with a verified source quote are scored; general good practice that the article does not state is not scored.
